programme.title: Anjelah Johnson-Reyes: Say I Won't
programme.desc: Filmed at the historic Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Anjelah Johnson-Reyes delivers her sixth stand-up special, covering big life moves, getting older, and the evolving stages of marriage, family, and friendship.

programme.title: Kelsey Cook: Mark Your Territory
programme.desc: Kelsey Cook recently relocated to Minnesota in the dead of winter to move in with her boyfriend. She covers the perks of dating an older man, the chaos of IUD insertions, navigating a parent with dementia, and much more.

programme.title: Matt Rife: Matthew Steven Rife
programme.desc: In his second self-produced hour special, built by friends and fans, Matt pushes comedic boundaries with stories, improv, and positive messages. A charismatic look into his wit, sharp humor, and crowd-driven energy.

programme.title: Kyle Kinane: Dirt Nap
programme.desc: Kinane explores tolerance and returning to his roots with self-deprecating humor, mining comedy from his suburban life after years on the road — from vegan quesadillas to the Fast and Furious franchise to life with a wayward cat.

programme.title: Matt Rife: Only Fans
programme.desc: Matt Rife's debut stand-up special, a culmination of his first ten years doing comedy starting at age 15. Fan-funded and self-produced, it showcases his sharp crowd work, edgy humor, and personal storytelling.

programme.title: Paul Foot: Dissolve
programme.desc: Paul Foot's most personal show ever. In 2022 something momentous changed for him, and in Dissolve he reveals how he discovered the secret of life — with inevitable detours through King Tutankhamun, Sir Cliff Richard, and officious lollipop ladies.

programme.title: Trae Crowder: Trash Daddy
programme.desc: Rural Tennessee's Trae Crowder brings his erudite-yet-trailer'y perspective to life, fatherhood, and America in the 2020s — from his experience as a displaced hillbilly in Hollywood to rednecks' complicated relationship with aliens.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Ron and Nancy are convinced that their new home is ideally suited to their budget. However, in the house, objects start to move by themselves and they later learn that their house is a way station between life and death.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: When a mother and a teenager are evicted from a townhouse in Montreal, the young girl commits suicide.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: On the banks of the Licking River, club owner Bobby Mackey has heard tales that the river draws murderers as well as Satanists to the area and that there have been times when the waters ran red with blood.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: A session with a Ouija board transforms Marie's home into a portal for the diabolical. The family realizes that the evil can lurk in the most ordinary places - and in the most innocent people.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Jan's seven-year-old son Cody begins communicating with an imaginary friend who lives in a red box in a nearby cemetery. Feeling helpless and desperate to protect her son, Jan contacts a shaman.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: With their first child on the way, Deb and Tony move in Atchison, Kansas. But when their son is born, the child's toys seem to take on a life of their own and strange whispers torment Tony.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In Taiwan, an American family refuses to believe there are ghosts in their house until their daughter becomes possessed. A Taoist priest explains that their house has been designed to empower the dead.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In Brookfield, Connecticut, young David suffers from intense nightmares and is physically attacked by an invisible entity. Paranormal investigators make contact with a legion of demons inside the child's body.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: An enigmatic photo of her boyfriend's brother killed in Vietnam entrances Lisa. As her obsession grows, she realizes that the spirit of the dead soldier is taking control of their lives.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In a small house in Glen Burnie, Maryland, unseen intruders attack 10-year-old Billy Bean. Billy struggles to learn the secrets of the house and fight them in any way he can - to save his sanity.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: When Clara and her family move into a small home in rural Hinsdale, New York, they realize that the peace of life in the country is merely an illusion - and the threat of death is very real.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Ed and Beth's ranch house seems like the perfect place to raise their toddler until they discover that they are not alone. A dark, heavy mist hangs over the house and grows larger day by day.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Following the breakup of his marriage, Steven LaChance begins to experience strange things inside his house.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: When Selena and her 3-year-old son move into an old house in Michigan, a series of photographs show what she cannot see with the naked eye: an evil face in the attic.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: After Mike and his girlfriend Lisa move in their new house, Lisa's personality begins to change dramatically.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Randy recites an incantation from a book on witchcraft, hoping to make contact with spirits of the dead.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: The Fahey family has lived in the same townhouse in the city of Galway, Irelan, for decades. But when a new baby arrives, he stirs up the psychic energy of a terrible crime committed many years ago.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: When April James and her fiance Matt buy a historic home in Salt Lake City, Utah, they immediately begin extensive work to make it their own, unaware of a ghostly inhabitant that detests change.

programme.desc: The new owners know that there is something strange about the Wheatsheaf Pub in Northern England. Behind the walls, they find bits of clothing and bones. Then, the pub itself begins to attack those within.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Mary Vogel has been a spiritual counselor for ten years, but a recent encounter with the demonic forces her to question everything she knows and trusts. Only an exorcism can save her soul.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Sarah Miller perceives that something supernatural lurks inside her new home, terrorizing her children.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Bobby and Addie Wilcott buy an historic house in New England, but experts discover a demonic presence.

programme.desc: Unsettling nightmares of a dark, angry figure plague Cindy as she prepares to move her family to an old house in her rural hometown. Soon after they settle in, reality begins to mirror her nightmares.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In 2003, when the Army deploys Randy and Marcy's son to the Middle East, Marcy is wracked with worry. As she reaches her emotional breaking point, a dormant spirit awakens to threaten her.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Since childhood, Rebecca has been able to see and hear spirits but has blocked their attempts to communicate.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Bill and Myrisa Spencer's new apartment is anything but quiet. Ghostly figures emerge from the shadows to roam the halls. Unable to break their lease, they are forced to coexist with the spirits.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Joanne and Jim Whitley buy an abandoned farm in New Hampshire. But soon, Joanne senses a negative presence nearby. When the presence turns physical, she calls on a Shamballa master.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Soon after the Shea family moves into an old home, eerie noises and ghostly voices puncture the quiet nights.

programme.desc: Sandra Waldron finds the supernatural realm fascinating. When she learns that her house is haunted, Sandra tries to perform Wiccan ceremonies and unwittingly opens a paranormal portal.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Shortly after moving in Vermont, the Johnson's daughter reveals that two fairies visit her room each night.

programme.desc: Stacy Jones has dedicated her life to helping others understand and cope with paranormal threats. When she witnesses a demon attacking her son, she enlists her colleague John Zaffis to save her son.

programme.title: A Haunting

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Eddie Benitez fears the spirit of a dead man who committed suicide is slowly killing his son. He turns to his Puerto Rican roots to combat the deadly ghost and save his family.

programme.desc: Morgan Knudsen and her friend Bob move into a flat in Edmonton. When a ghost attacks her, she calls in a demonologist who reveals the entity is trying to drive her out so that it can possess Bob.

programme.desc: Three teenage boys, with little else to do in the small town of Green Lake, Wisconsin, decide to spend Halloween night in the reputedly haunted Dartford Cemetery.

programme.desc: Faced with a supernatural threat, Betty Johnson and her family move, hoping to leave their troubles behind.

programme.desc: Connecticut natives Lynn and Jason Ryder purchase a historic restaurant, thinking it will be an adventure.

programme.title: Season of the Witch
programme.desc: Fourteenth century knights transport a suspected witch to a monastery, where monks deduce her powers could be the source of the Black Plague.

programme.title: Aurora - Fire in the Sky
programme.desc: In the earth’s polar regions, a ghostly flicker and colourful glow often brighten the night sky. Whoever sees an aurora event will never forget this impressive experience. Finland’s Saami people, Alaska’s Inuit, Canada’s Native Americans and New Zealand’s Maori all have legends about the origins and meaning of this magic natural spectacle. These stories tell of spirits dancing in the sky, of a bright and better world where hunting game is abundant, of battling gods and celestial messages.

programme.title: Faroe Islands - A Secret Beauty
programme.desc: The Faroe Islands in the North Atlantic, located in the middle of the Gulf Stream between Scotland and Iceland, are an archipelago of eighteen green volcanic islands where a unique culture has developed over the last thousand years. As direct descendants of the Vikings, the Faroese feel committed to their traditions and hold on to customs, without missing out on the advantages of the modern and globalised world - from archaic hunter and shepherd culture to contemporary art. With the highest birth rate in Europe and the lowest social inequality in the world, the just fifty thousand Faroese are a very special people living on one of the last natural paradises in Europe.

programme.title: Gronland - In the Glare of Ice
programme.desc: Greenland is the largest island in the world and the landmass closest to the North Pole. 80% of the country is covered by a layer of ice up to 3000 meters thick. Most of the inhabitants of the country are spread over the breathtaking landscape of the ice-free west coast. The country is mostly inhabited by Inuit, who have been feeding on what nature has provided them for thousands of years. But the original life is in a state of change. The modernisation of society and man-made global warming threaten the Arctic natural paradise that is so incredibly important for our planet. Through the eyes of locals we get to know the authentic Greenland.

programme.title: Iceland - On Top of the World
programme.desc: A scenic expedition through majestic volcanoes, seething geysers, powerful waterfalls, threatening fjords and almighty glaciers. Hardly any other country offers such a variety of spectacular forces of nature! We will give you an insight on how it can be that the people of a small, distant island with only a fraction of sunlight in some months are happier than the people in more sun-blessed countries.

programme.title: mareTV: Sweden's High Coast
programme.desc: Sweden's Höga Kusten (High Coast) has been rising by almost one centimetre per year since the last ice age 10,000 years ago. This has created a hilly Baltic Sea landscape on the Gulf of Bothnia with small and large islands. Untouched nature, dense forests and energetic, rather idiosyncratic islanders have plenty of room there. Every year at the end of August a biting stench mixes with the fresh Baltic Sea breeze. For weeks the so-called sour herring, Swedish: Surströmming, is fermented in brine. Ruben Madsen is a producer of surströmming and an absolute connoisseur. In his wooden hut on the island of Ulvön he puts the herring in according to a traditional recipe. At the start of the season, the cans are opened for the first time. Lovers of the "stinky fish" then come from all over the world to taste the now world-famous delicacy in cans. Opening the cans of "rotten fish" is considered internationally as a test of courage, people film themselves doing so, the inhabitants of the High Coast can only smile about it.

programme.title: Wild Skagerrak
programme.desc: The strait that connects the North Sea with the Baltic, with depths of over 700 metres, is notorious for its dangerously strong currents. But currents also mean food and therefore nourishment for the large swarms of fish that inhabit the region. The sea grass meadows are comparable with those off the Californian coast. Harbour seals, grey seals and orcas hunt here, as do the rare black mouth cat shark and porpoises. Close by, catfish mate, which in itself is quite spectacular and never caught on film in this way before. Lion's mane jellyfish with nettle threads of up to 30 metres in length make their way through the open sea. Skagerrak's coastal regions are amongst the most beautiful and varied in Europe and boast one of the world's great bird paradises. Oystercatchers, sandwich and arctic terns are more plentiful here than anywhere else in Europe. The infinitely long dune landscape of the Skagerrak, is Denmark's answer to the skerries of the Swedish and Norwegian coasts. Large seal colonies can be found in the isolation of the small, picturesque islands and one can come face to face with the animals. In this rough, yet infinitely beautiful landscape, the many streams and rivers that open out into the Skagerrak, are quite remarkable. We accompany salmon in an equally beautiful river landscape and meet with ospreys and sea eagles and eventually come face to face with a brown bear mother and her little ones.

programme.title: One Year in Norway's Lofoten
programme.sub-title: S01 : E01 One Year in Norway's Lofoten: Episode 1
programme.desc: Winter means more than just the beginning of the year for the people of Lofoten: For more than a thousand years, Lofoten has been a hub for cod fishing, with seasons lasting from February to April as huge shoals migrate from the Barents Sea to these waters. During these hectic months, more than 65,000 tons of fish are brought to shore, securing the income for the whole of Lofoten for years to come. Around a quarter of the fish caught ends up on lines to dry upon racks. From a young age, the children from the fishing villages get to earn some pocket money by cutting cod tongues and selling the produce as a delicacy appreciated by the locals.

programme.title: One Year in Norway's Lofoten
programme.sub-title: S01 : E02 One Year in Norway's Lofoten: Episode 2
programme.desc: Almost unnoticeably, spring turns into summer. The days become longer and longer, with a never-setting sun. People who have spent their winter and spring working hard can finally enjoy their own nature, even though the temperature is only slightly warmer. Lofoten is sparsely populated, just 24,000 people live here. Unstad is one of its smallest communities with only 15 inhabitants, but despite that, it has become a hotspot for arctic surf and is host to the northern-most surf center in the world. Surfers from all over the globe come to surf in the arctic water.

programme.title: Europe's far North - Lofoten and the Arctic Ocean
programme.desc: Lofoten is the rugged archipelago in the Norwegian Arctic Ocean. Whoever arrives here is really at the end. Moskenes is the end of the line, and anyone who wants to go further needs a boat or a plane. The only way to get to the open sea is via the Maelstrom, which is quite dangerous. On the outermost headland, there are only a few ruins left. The last inhabitants are long gone, a supply was hardly possible. But fishermen are on the way, mainly to catch cod. And there is the coastal administration, which takes care of broken sea marks and lighthouses. A visit to one of the luxurious ships of the Hurtig Line is not to be missed. They shuttle off rough coasts on an eleven-day trip between the Russian border and southern Norway. A floating workplace for a wide variety of professions. The island of Andøya is not served by the Hurtiglinie. It lies too far out in the Atlantic. One of the most important observatories in Europe is located here. A young woman, Sandra Blindheim, is the boss. She is responsible for the large laser that delivers important information to scientists around the world. On clear winter nights, there is a wonderful panoramic view of the aurora borealis.

programme.title: Winter Journey to the Polar Circle (Exploring Norway on the Nordlandsbanen)
programme.desc: The Nordland Railway in Norway, travels from Trondheim through the isolated regions of Trendelag and Nordland. After Mo I Rana, it traverses the Arctic Circle and ends in the northern Norwegian town of Bodø. The railway covers a distance of some 729 kilometres, passing by dense, snow-covered forests, frozen fjords and snow-capped mountains. Temperatures of sometimes minus 30 degrees are quite normal here for months, on many days there is no more than five hours of daylight. Kindergarten teacher Kaia Aarstrand und her husband, Bjørnar, a technician for the municipality, live with their four boys in Aursletta, deep within the Vistenfjord, far away from civilization. All made possible by the Norwegian state: electricity, mobile phone connection and a speedboat that brings the family to school and to work. But when the Vistenfjord freezes up, the family is isolated for days. Tormod Schøning spends hours on end on his Saltfjellet whenever snowstorms occur and he has to clear the only road connection between North and South Norway with his snow plough. For the duration of his shifts, Tormod lives in the snow plough station.

But currents also mean food and therefore nourishment for the large swarms of fish that inhabit the region. The sea grass meadows are comparable with those off the Californian coast. Harbour seals, grey seals and orcas hunt here, as do the rare black mouth cat shark and porpoises. Close by, catfish mate, which in itself is quite spectacular and never caught on film in this way before. Lion's mane jellyfish with nettle threads of up to 30 metres in length make their way through the open sea. Skagerrak's coastal regions are amongst the most beautiful and varied in Europe and boast one of the world's great bird paradises. Oystercatchers, sandwich and arctic terns are more plentiful here than anywhere else in Europe. The infinitely long dune landscape of the Skagerrak, is Denmark's answer to the skerries of the Swedish and Norwegian coasts. Large seal colonies can be found in the isolation of the small, picturesque islands and one can come face to face with the animals. In this rough, yet infinitely beautiful landscape, the many streams and rivers that open out into the Skagerrak, are quite remarkable. We accompany salmon in an equally beautiful river landscape and meet with ospreys and sea eagles and eventually come face to face with a brown bear mother and her little ones.

programme.title: One Year in Norway's Lofoten
programme.sub-title: S01 : E01 One Year in Norway's Lofoten: Episode 1
programme.desc: Winter means more than just the beginning of the year for the people of Lofoten: For more than a thousand years, Lofoten has been a hub for cod fishing, with seasons lasting from February to April as huge shoals migrate from the Barents Sea to these waters. During these hectic months, more than 65,000 tons of fish are brought to shore, securing the income for the whole of Lofoten for years to come. Around a quarter of the fish caught ends up on lines to dry upon racks. From a young age, the children from the fishing villages get to earn some pocket money by cutting cod tongues and selling the produce as a delicacy appreciated by the locals.

programme.title: One Year in Norway's Lofoten
programme.sub-title: S01 : E02 One Year in Norway's Lofoten: Episode 2
programme.desc: Almost unnoticeably, spring turns into summer. The days become longer and longer, with a never-setting sun. People who have spent their winter and spring working hard can finally enjoy their own nature, even though the temperature is only slightly warmer. Lofoten is sparsely populated, just 24,000 people live here. Unstad is one of its smallest communities with only 15 inhabitants, but despite that, it has become a hotspot for arctic surf and is host to the northern-most surf center in the world. Surfers from all over the globe come to surf in the arctic water.

programme.title: Europe's far North - Lofoten and the Arctic Ocean
programme.desc: Lofoten is the rugged archipelago in the Norwegian Arctic Ocean. Whoever arrives here is really at the end. Moskenes is the end of the line, and anyone who wants to go further needs a boat or a plane. The only way to get to the open sea is via the Maelstrom, which is quite dangerous. On the outermost headland, there are only a few ruins left. The last inhabitants are long gone, a supply was hardly possible. But fishermen are on the way, mainly to catch cod. And there is the coastal administration, which takes care of broken sea marks and lighthouses. A visit to one of the luxurious ships of the Hurtig Line is not to be missed. They shuttle off rough coasts on an eleven-day trip between the Russian border and southern Norway. A floating workplace for a wide variety of professions. The island of Andøya is not served by the Hurtiglinie. It lies too far out in the Atlantic. One of the most important observatories in Europe is located here. A young woman, Sandra Blindheim, is the boss. She is responsible for the large laser that delivers important information to scientists around the world. On clear winter nights, there is a wonderful panoramic view of the aurora borealis.

programme.title: Winter Journey to the Polar Circle (Exploring Norway on the Nordlandsbanen)
programme.desc: The Nordland Railway in Norway, travels from Trondheim through the isolated regions of Trendelag and Nordland. After Mo I Rana, it traverses the Arctic Circle and ends in the northern Norwegian town of Bodø. The railway covers a distance of some 729 kilometres, passing by dense, snow-covered forests, frozen fjords and snow-capped mountains. Temperatures of sometimes minus 30 degrees are quite normal here for months, on many days there is no more than five hours of daylight. Kindergarten teacher Kaia Aarstrand und her husband, Bjørnar, a technician for the municipality, live with their four boys in Aursletta, deep within the Vistenfjord, far away from civilization. All made possible by the Norwegian state: electricity, mobile phone connection and a speedboat that brings the family to school and to work. But when the Vistenfjord freezes up, the family is isolated for days. Tormod Schøning spends hours on end on his Saltfjellet whenever snowstorms occur and he has to clear the only road connection between North and South Norway with his snow plough. For the duration of his shifts, Tormod lives in the snow plough station.

programme.title: Aurora - Fire in the Sky
programme.desc: In the earth’s polar regions, a ghostly flicker and colourful glow often brighten the night sky. Whoever sees an aurora event will never forget this impressive experience. Finland’s Saami people, Alaska’s Inuit, Canada’s Native Americans and New Zealand’s Maori all have legends about the origins and meaning of this magic natural spectacle. These stories tell of spirits dancing in the sky, of a bright and better world where hunting game is abundant, of battling gods and celestial messages.

programme.title: Faroe Islands - A Secret Beauty
programme.desc: The Faroe Islands in the North Atlantic, located in the middle of the Gulf Stream between Scotland and Iceland, are an archipelago of eighteen green volcanic islands where a unique culture has developed over the last thousand years. As direct descendants of the Vikings, the Faroese feel committed to their traditions and hold on to customs, without missing out on the advantages of the modern and globalised world - from archaic hunter and shepherd culture to contemporary art. With the highest birth rate in Europe and the lowest social inequality in the world, the just fifty thousand Faroese are a very special people living on one of the last natural paradises in Europe.

programme.title: Gronland - In the Glare of Ice
programme.desc: Greenland is the largest island in the world and the landmass closest to the North Pole. 80% of the country is covered by a layer of ice up to 3000 meters thick. Most of the inhabitants of the country are spread over the breathtaking landscape of the ice-free west coast. The country is mostly inhabited by Inuit, who have been feeding on what nature has provided them for thousands of years. But the original life is in a state of change. The modernisation of society and man-made global warming threaten the Arctic natural paradise that is so incredibly important for our planet. Through the eyes of locals we get to know the authentic Greenland.

programme.title: Iceland - On Top of the World
programme.desc: A scenic expedition through majestic volcanoes, seething geysers, powerful waterfalls, threatening fjords and almighty glaciers. Hardly any other country offers such a variety of spectacular forces of nature! We will give you an insight on how it can be that the people of a small, distant island with only a fraction of sunlight in some months are happier than the people in more sun-blessed countries.

programme.title: mareTV: Sweden's High Coast
programme.desc: Sweden's Höga Kusten (High Coast) has been rising by almost one centimetre per year since the last ice age 10,000 years ago. This has created a hilly Baltic Sea landscape on the Gulf of Bothnia with small and large islands. Untouched nature, dense forests and energetic, rather idiosyncratic islanders have plenty of room there. Every year at the end of August a biting stench mixes with the fresh Baltic Sea breeze. For weeks the so-called sour herring, Swedish: Surströmming, is fermented in brine. Ruben Madsen is a producer of surströmming and an absolute connoisseur. In his wooden hut on the island of Ulvön he puts the herring in according to a traditional recipe. At the start of the season, the cans are opened for the first time. Lovers of the "stinky fish" then come from all over the world to taste the now world-famous delicacy in cans. Opening the cans of "rotten fish" is considered internationally as a test of courage, people film themselves doing so, the inhabitants of the High Coast can only smile about it.

programme.title: 15th Meridian East - Similarity in Difference
programme.desc: Almost 11000 kilometres lie between the northernmost and southernmost point of the 15th meridian east. Here you will find extreme landscapes such as the shimmering heat of Africa or the eternal cold of northern Scandinavia. Five people from Spitsbergen, Namibia, Slovenia, Germany and Poland dedicate their lives to environmental protection.

programme.title: 15th Meridian East - Similarity in Difference
programme.sub-title: S01 : E03 Sow, Harvest, Eat – Our Conservatory
programme.desc: This episode focuses on people from five countries who share a common passion: The production of their own food and food. What culinary treasures are hidden in the different regions, from Spitsbergen to Sweden, Austria, Poland and Chad?

programme.title: Rewilding: Back to Nature
programme.desc: Worldwide, there are various projects and approaches to give nature more space again. The aim is to create larger wilderness areas that develop with hardly any influence of humans - by reintroducing so-called key animal species and creating a network of wilderness corridors across entire continents. Rewilding promises to be a cost-effective form of conservation in which we can boost biodiversity and protect the climate.

programme.title: Poppy's Promise - Secret Life in a Cornfield
programme.desc: The cornfield - just an area for producing food… or a land full of secrets? This doc portrays a little recognized habitat right next door. The spectacular visuals filmed with state of the art equipment introduce the surprisingly large diversity of field inhabitants. We follow a hamster family through a season full of adventures and are drawn into an unknown world – a world of which we thought we knew everything about. In the western industrial nations cornfields and woods take up the greatest proportion of rural land. But how much natural life dwells in a cornfield? Why are some cornfield inhabitants harmful and others useful and what do the colourful flowers at the edge of the field promise us? We follow a hamster family through a season full of adventures and are drawn into an unknown world – a world of which we thought we knew everything about.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.sub-title: S02 : E02 The Racing Cyclists Of Burundi
programme.desc: The racing cyclists of Burundi have a dangerous job. But it’s a vital one for Burundi’s economy. Bicycles are the main means of transportation in one of the smallest countries in Africa. Bananas, the staple food in Burundi, are transported from the markets to a banana beer brewing factory. We accompany Tharcien, a bike courier, on his exhausting cross country trip on the Burundi Highway.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.sub-title: S02 : E01 The Road To Death In The Andes
programme.desc: The Carretera de la muerte - the road to death- is one of the most dangerous roads in the world. Year after year many people die here. We accompany trucker Omar and his co-driver Jaime on their trip across the Andes, encountering cyclists, mountain bikers and coca-farmers on the way.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The Sichuan Tibet Highway is the road of longing for many. It leads through fascinating landscapes and remote areas up to the Himalayan Mountains. We accompany truck driver Ren Taiping on his trip to the Tibetan capital city of Lhasa, encountering pilgrims, mountain bikers and nomads on this dangerous journey.

programme.title: Caribbean sisters: The Lesser Antilles St. Kitts & Nevis
programme.desc: In the centre of the Caribbean, volcanoes rise steeply from the sea, thus shaping the sister islands of St. Kitts & Nevis. Their slopes, covered in lush rainforests, snow-white, sandy beaches and the surrounding tur-quoise tinted waters provide the ultimate setting for this record-breaking, albeit tiny island paradise: Both islets are the smallest of the Caribbean dwarf states and also rank among the world’s ten smallest states. A hot pepper sauce, made of a creative mixture of ginger, garlic, thyme and extraordinarily hot chillies that thrive in the hot and humid climate of Nevis, is simmering on the stove of Violet and Llewellyn’s house. Lemmy Pemberton digs up abandoned turtle nests with his bare hands, as he wants to be certain that all of the babies have indeed managed to make it. Members of the Turtle Group catch sea turtles in order to take their measurements and fit them with transmitters. Taxi bus-es are not only the main means of transport on St. Kitts & Nevis, they are also an artistic expression of each driver’s personality. Colourfully embellished, each taxi represents island art on wheels.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.sub-title: S01 : E07 America's National Parks - Olympic
programme.desc: Olympic National Park is an American national park located in the State of Washington, on the Olympic Peninsula. The park has four regions: the Pacific coastline, alpine areas, the west side temperate rainforest and the forests of the drier east side. Within the park there are three distinct ecosystems which are subalpine forest and wildflower meadow, temperate forest, and the rugged Pacific coast. President Theodore Roosevelt originally designated Mount Olympus National Monument on 2 March 1909. The monument was redesignated as a national park by Congress and President Franklin Roosevelt on June 29, 1938. In 1976, Olympic National Park was designated by UNESCO as an International Biosphere Reserve, and in 1981 as a World Heritage Site. In 1988, Congress designated 95 percent of the park as the Olympic Wilderness.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.sub-title: S01 : E08 America's National Parks - Yosemite
programme.desc: Yosemite National Park is a place of superlatives: with towering cliffs and giant sequoias, home to coyotes, black bears and the most elusive of all: the bobcat. Watch this documentary with ist spectacular shots, aerial views and time-lapse shots and learn some new facts about the biodiversity in one of North Americas most spectacular National Parks.

programme.title: Wild Prairie Man
programme.desc: Located in the Northern Great Plains of Canada, Grasslands National Park has been a 20 year odyssey for wildlife photographer James R. Page. For James, critters are more interesting than people and he shares some of his iconic images and experiences from this endangered ecosystem. We showcase the parks wilderness that is dominated by prairie light and dark sky, the wildlife, prairie dogs, mesmerizing landscapes, and bisons. We immerse ourselves in the wild habitat of Grasslands National Park for over a year capturing some never before scenes in the Wild Prairie. James R. Page's connection to the land and the wildlife provides an unforgettable journey into the heart of this endangered ecosystem, while Park experts help us understand its complexity.

programme.title: Winter Journey to the Polar Circle (Exploring Norway on the Nordlandsbanen)
programme.desc: The Nordland Railway in Norway, travels from Trondheim through the isolated regions of Trendelag and Nordland. After Mo I Rana, it traverses the Arctic Circle and ends in the northern Norwegian town of Bodø. The railway covers a distance of some 729 kilometres, passing by dense, snow-covered forests, frozen fjords and snow-capped mountains. Temperatures of sometimes minus 30 degrees are quite normal here for months, on many days there is no more than five hours of daylight. Kindergarten teacher Kaia Aarstrand und her husband, Bjørnar, a technician for the municipality, live with their four boys in Aursletta, deep within the Vistenfjord, far away from civilization. All made possible by the Norwegian state: electricity, mobile phone connection and a speedboat that brings the family to school and to work. But when the Vistenfjord freezes up, the family is isolated for days. Tormod Schøning spends hours on end on his Saltfjellet whenever snowstorms occur and he has to clear the only road connection between North and South Norway with his snow plough. For the duration of his shifts, Tormod lives in the snow plough station.

programme.title: Wild Slovakia
programme.desc: Brown bears, wolves, lynx, eagles… where within the European Union are these carnivores still regular inhabitants? Where can you find mountainous regions that yet wait to be discovered by mass tourism?

programme.title: mareTV: Peru - Coast of the Incas
programme.desc: Dramatically, the coast plunges into the sea, the so-called Costa of Peru is a gigantic desert on the Pacific Ocean, 2,400 kilometers long. Rugged, bizarre, like from another star. Ancient cultures settled here, the Moche and the Chimú. Later the proud Inca, the self-proclaimed royal people of the Andes, ruled. In the small town of Huanchaco in northern Peru, the fishermen build a new boat every month: from reed. The small ships are called Caballito de Totora (reed horses), because the shape is reminiscent of a horse and the fishermen ride in it kneeling in the waves. About 2,000 years ago, the moche used it to go out to sea. Carlos Segura Azola is a descendant of the moche. He is currently building a "reed horse" again. But actually something completely different occupies him. Carlos has been afraid of the sea ever since his father drowned at work. The fisherman consults a Brucha, a witch. She tries to drive him out of panic at the Pacific with mysterious ceremonies. At some point Carlos' reed boat is finished and he has to get out to his nets again. In the south, in the port city of Pisco, there are hardly any private cars. Mototaxis on three wheels are the means of transport here. Every moto looks different, because the young drivers compete with each other. They constantly pimp out their tricycles with spoilers, mirrors and all kinds of decorations. Because if you stand out in the traffic jam, you get the most passengers. But nowhere else in Peru is road traffic as dense and chaotic as in the capital Lima. That's why Juan Ortiz goes daily with his Delta glider over the coastal road into the air. He is the flying reporter and reports live for the traffic news. And he is not alone with his aircraft. Dozens of paragliders float along the cliffs of Lima at any time of the day. The Pacific provides a constant upwind on the up to 160 meter high cliffs. Somewhere in the labyrinth of the metropolis of millions hundreds of believers trot to the beat of the music of a Jesus statue on the cross. A procession for the "Lord of Miracles", the brass band intones church songs. The music student Bruno Alvarado drags and plays the largest instrument, a sousaphone. Every day there are dozens of processions in Lima. Practical for Bruno, he finances his studies with the musical accompaniment. Away from the hustle and bustle of the big city, in the Paracas National Park, it is deserted. Luis Zapato runs a kiosk on a lonely beach amidst huge sand dunes. The kiosk has meanwhile developed into a gourmet temple, even the capital city dwellers flock here. Especially because of the scallops that Luis is the only licence holder to collect far and wide from the seabed. Inti Mar he called his beach snack, Inti is the sun god, Mar the sea. At Luis you literally eat like a sun god at the sea. This is only possible here, on the Inca coast.

programme.title: mareTV: Mexico's Caribbean Coast
programme.desc: The palm tree laden beaches on Mexico's Riviera Maya on the Yucatan peninsula are endless, and the turquoise sea with its gentle Caribbean surf is a warm 25 degrees during the mild winter in this part of the world. Between Cancún and Punta Allen, where once there was little more than bushland and a few sleepy fishing villages, vibrant life has evolved during the past three decades. Richard Sowa has lived on a floating island for the past 15 years: an island he built himself out of empty plastic bottles. The bon vivant him-self sees it as a "solution for our planet's refuse problem". Off Punta Allen, a village in the bay of Sian Ka'an, Mexican Mara Coral Ley and her cousin Kim, continue to catch lobsters by adhering to the traditional method and were awarded an "Eco seal for sustainable fishing" for their trouble. It is silent under water off Isla Mujeres and it is here that the artist Jason deCaires has constructed a sculpture park. Hundreds of lifesize figures form an artificial reef at a depth of 12 metres. Fish and plants complete his work of art. The master himself is convinced: "Mother Nature is the true artist".

programme.title: glCuba - Brilliantly Caribbean
programme.desc: Even anyone who has not yet been to Cuba can conjure up certain images of American vintage street cruisers, imposing buildings that have seen better days, white sandy beaches full of palms and loving couples on the Malecón against a backdrop of crashing waves. This island is somewhat of a myth and its people generate a special joie de vivre. The legendary Hershey Train departs for Matanzas from the capital, Havana. On the oldest electrified railway line in the Caribbean, 60-year-old Spanish carriages make their way along al-most 100 kilometres of coastline in the most relaxed way possible. The Salvavidas on Varadero, probably the most famous beach on the island, have a particular-ly beautiful workplace. The lifeguards' territory ex-tends for more than 20 kilometres. In order to protect the coasts of Cuba, mangroves have been replanted here for many years. The project is supported by the UN and planting is often carried out by schoolchildren. In doing so, Cuban children learn how to treat their maritime habitat in a sustainable fashion. The former colonial city of Trinidad on Cuba's south coast is gen-erally considered to be one of the most beautiful places in the entire Caribbean. The houses here are particular-ly colourful. A plethora of magnificent buildings can be seen at the Plaza Mayor, the neo-baroque main square.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.sub-title: S01 : E03 Lahemaa National Park, Estonia
programme.desc: Lahemaa National Park on Estonias Baltic coast features ancient forests, rivers and peninsulas where nature has remained largely untouched.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.desc: The Curonian Spit is a narrow peninsula of dunes and forests shaped by destruction and recovery through careful human intervention.

programme.title: The U.S. East Coast
programme.sub-title: S01 : E04 The U.S. East Coast, Surf And Turf
programme.desc: New Hampshire has only 19 kilometers of coastline and short summers, all the more reason Shauna Fraser takes every opportunity to be by the sea. In the sheltered harbor of Rye, Shauna also targets inner attitude with yoga on a paddleboard.

programme.title: The U.S. East Coast
programme.sub-title: S01 : E05 The U.S. East Coast, The Southern States
programme.desc: We travel from Georgia through the Carolinas to Virginia, ending near Washington, DC. Along the way we meet a Georgia farmer; talk to painter J. Chris Wilson in Charleston; sail along the Outer Banks of Carolina, and visit rural Virginia, experiencing life in the beautiful southern states.

programme.title: mareTV: The Eckernförde Bay - Beach shooters, mine clearance divers, squirrels
programme.desc: Fjord, ford, bay, gulf: there are many names for the beautiful extensions of the Baltic Sea into the country. Eckernförde Bay is shaped by currents, surf and people. It stretches 17 kilometers to the town that gives it its name. Stephan Möller is the acting shooting master of the Eckernförder Bürgerschützengilde. He spent a whole year preparing the beach shooting festival and then this: fog, rain and a stiff breeze. Traditionally, the Eckernförde marksmen always shoot at a wooden bird in the direction of the sea at Whitsun. Under strict conditions! And these stipulate a clear view of at least one kilometer out into the bay. The event literally threatens to fall through, for the first time in 449 years. Around 3,000 soldiers are stationed at the Eckernförde naval base, but only a small group is allowed to call itself an elite unit: the mine divers. They are considered the toughest soldiers in the Navy. Anyone who wants to be one of them has to undergo extreme training. This year, just two candidates made it to the final round. Now they still have to pass the dreaded final exam: running 20 kilometers with marching gear and then swimming ten kilometers through Eckernförde Bay.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The Parque Nacional Peneda-Gerês is the only national park in Portugal. An area of almost 700 square kilometers, located in the extreme north of Portugal. Barren and rocky ridges in the plateaus, contrast with large forests and lush ground vegetation in deep valleys, crossed by lakes and rivers. The park is known for its oak forests, which are predominantly pedunculate and Pyrenean oaks. Among the typical animals of the park are the small Garrano ponies, a very old breed of horse and the only one in Europe that still lives in the wild.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The highest mountain range in Portugal is the Serra da Estrela. The episode embarks on a voyage of discovery to adventurous rock formations and villages steeped in tradition. The nature park is the largest protected area on the Iberian peninsula. In the mountain range we accompany the young scientist Ana Matos, who wants to breathe new life into old traditions, and cheese maker Maria Natália Lopes. She watches over more than 350 sheeps.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.sub-title: S01 : E03 South West Portugal: Alentejano and Costa Vicentina
programme.desc: In the southwest of Portugal lies the little known Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina. It encompasses a narrow coastal strip that runs along the coast to the south of Portugal. Sparsely populated, this coastal region, which was placed under protection in 1988, is considered one of the last intact ecosystems in Europe. The steep cliffs, the almost constant wind and high waves have ensured that mass tourism has not gained a foothold here. There are still near-natural forests and a diverse bird life.

programme.title: Model And The Bushmen, The
programme.desc: This is the story of an incredible adventure: a young woman from Norway moves into the wild and joins the last Bushmen hunters in Namibia. Every morning, the women set out to forage and the men sneak into the bush to hunt, carrying little else but homemade bows and arrows as they walk through the wilderness.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - The Line Goes Dead - E513
programme.desc: When the severed head of a wife and mother is found, Lt. Joe Kenda uses forensics and interrogation to find both her body and her killer. Then… a young man’s murder looks like a robbery gone wrong until Kenda learns the odd reason he’s living there.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - My My, Merry Christmas - E203
programme.desc: Donald Ott is found shot to death, friends tell police he didnít have an enemy in the world. But when Lt. Joe Kenda speaks with family, he learns of a relative who might hold the key to the mystery.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Murder Bites - E205
programme.desc: A young woman is found naked and strangled in a park not 200 yards from her home. It isnít until Lt. Joe Kenda rethinks the entire case that he realizes someone has been lying.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Death Rains Down - E209
programme.desc: Restaurant worker Sharon Coleman is murdered in a hail of large caliber gunfire. Kenda must break through a web of lies to hunt down one of the most dangerous criminal masterminds heís ever faced.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - A Prayer for the Dying - E311
programme.sub-title: S3:E311 A Prayer for the Dying
programme.desc: A mother of two is found dead in the most expensive part of Colorado Springs, leaving Lt. Joe Kenda stumped -- until lhe looks into her personal life.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Murder Bites - E205
programme.desc: A young woman is found naked and strangled in a park not 200 yards from her home. It isnít until Lt. Joe Kenda rethinks the entire case that he realizes someone has been lying.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Blood Sisters - E213
programme.desc: The bullet-ridden bodies of two sisters are found in a suburban house thatís littered with mysterious clues. Joe Kenda learns that the two unassuming young mothers shared an explosive secret.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Gut Instinct - E618
programme.desc: When a soon-to-be grandmother doesn’t come home from work, her daughter knows something terrible must have happened and reports her missing. As the investigation unfolds, Lt. Joe Kenda realizes they could be dealing with a fledgling serial killer.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Officer Down - E518
programme.desc: Sgt. Joe Kenda is faced with his worst nightmare when he learns a friend and fellow officer, Mark Dabling, has been killed in the line of duty. Police conduct an all-out manhunt and discover the gunman is even more dangerous than they’d thought.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Bad Blood - E401
programme.desc: A popular army vet is found bleeding on the cold asphalt of a parking lot -- his chest littered with too many knife wounds to count. Kenda’s case is stuck in first gear until a clue leads to an unlikely killer.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Gut Instinct - E618
programme.desc: When a soon-to-be grandmother doesn’t come home from work, her daughter knows something terrible must have happened and reports her missing. As the investigation unfolds, Lt. Joe Kenda realizes they could be dealing with a fledgling serial killer.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Follow the Money - E711
programme.desc: The body of a 72-year-old man is found in junkyard, stabbed 13 times and wearing nothing but his underwear and dentures. When investigators discover a trail of purchases made with the victim’s credit card, they hope it will lead them to the killer.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Point of No Return - E413
programme.desc: When an explosion rocks a sleepy suburb, it’s up to Kenda to ID the charred remains and find the killer who triggered the blast. Then… a young mother’s murder leads the CSPD on a harrowing car chase that ends in a violent showdown.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - A Gathering of Evil - E104
programme.desc: Teen runaway Maggie Fetty is found strangled to death on a mountain road. An anonymous tipster blames Maggieís best friend, but she accuses a mental patient with multiple personalities.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Door No. 12 - E405
programme.desc: Neighbors are stunned when Louis Matos and Colleen Johnson are gunned down for no apparent reason. After a series of false leads, Kenda locates a panic-stricken eyewitness.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Time Bomb - E612
programme.desc: In 1978, Lt. Joe Kenda is new to the CSPD, and gets more than he bargains for when a local bank is the target of a massive explosion. But is it an isolated incident, or the opening move in a frightening wave terror to descend upon Colorado Springs?

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Married to the Job - E719
programme.desc: Sgt. Joe Kenda and his officers are facing off against a barricaded gunman when he gets an emergency call from his wife. Kathy winds up overhearing him being shot at, leading her to grapple with the terrifying realities of being married to a cop.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Shallow Grave - E712
programme.desc: Lt. Joe Kenda and his team investigate the scene of an apparent suicide, only to be forced to flee when they discover the house is booby-trapped. Then… Kenda is nearly stumped when a group of teens discover human bones on the outskirts of town.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Blood From a Stone - E707
programme.desc: A bystander receives a deadly head injury during a roadside altercation, but the stakes are raised when his body disappears from the scene. Then… when a toddler is kidnapped for ransom, Kenda joins forces with an undercover team in a desperate race against time.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Bring My Baby Home - E620
programme.desc: A four-week-old girl is kidnapped, leaving her mother in anguish and police scrambling to find her. As days go by with no sign of the baby or demands for ransom, sergeants Joe Kenda and Robert Sapp fear she’s been sold on the black market… or worse.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - My Worst Fear - E519
programme.desc: Police are shocked to find a 13-year-old boy killed in an explosion, but their grief turns to alarm when they discover a second, unexploded bomb. To catch the killer, Det. Joe Kenda must first figure out whom the bomb was meant for.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Timothy Peart's Last Dance - E615
programme.desc: When a teen is killed at a party, police question the guests and wonder if they’re all part of a cover-up. Then… A reported suicide leaves Kenda with doubts. Did the victim take his life to end his troubles, or did his troubled past catch up to him?

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Raise the Dead - E604
programme.desc: When 71-year-old Orville Head passes away, no one questions the death of an elderly man with health problems. But when a tip comes in suggesting foul play, Lt. Joe Kenda is left with only one way to reveal the truth: exhume the body from its grave.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Bad Moon Rising - E601
programme.desc: On the night before Halloween, a real-life nightmare unfolds when a young man is found clinging to life. The case takes a dark turn when Lt. Joe Kenda learns there is a second victim somewhere in the woods. Can police rescue him before it’s too late?

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - After School Special - E607
programme.desc: Tragedy strikes when a beloved teacher is poisoned in her classroom. As doctors fight to save Barbara Lewis’ life, Lt. Joe Kenda and his team delve into her personal affairs looking for clues… but the biggest revelation comes from the poison itself.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - With Friends Like This - E713
programme.desc: A young man is found gunned down outside his home after a day spent helping friends move apartments. Sgt. Joe Kenda and Det. John Anderson must determine whether the killer was a complete stranger, a barrio gang member, or a jealous lover.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - The Girl Next Door - E703
programme.desc: When a young army vet is found stabbed to death on his living room floor, suspicions quickly fall to a neighbor who was arrested during a nearby altercation. But when Kenda takes a closer look at the victim’s love life, he realizes someone’s been lying.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Knock Knock - E603
programme.desc: A gathering of friends turns deadly when two gunmen shoot William Davis in the head. When the witnesses are unable to provide any solid leads, Lt. Joe Kenda and his team dig into his past and start to suspect someone in William’s circle is lying.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Fractured Glass - E705
programme.desc: When affable ladies’ man Michael Tittemore is gunned down in the dead of night, Kenda first sets his sights on the roommates who were present during the murder. But a shocking revelation will turn his attention to a far more nefarious band of suspects.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Hail of Bullets - E708
programme.desc: The murder of a young father stuns his close-knit community, but the investigation reveals a neighborly dispute turned deadly. Then…when a house is besieged by mysterious gunfire, Kenda enlists a team of specialists to trace the bullets’ origin.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - Bad Things Come in Threes - E306
programme.sub-title: S3:E306 Bad Things Come in Threes
programme.desc: When two young mothers are gunned down behind a crowded bar, Kenda has to first determine who was the intended target and who was collateral damage.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - John 3:16 - E613
programme.desc: A man rushes his friend to the hospital with serious gunshot wounds, reporting they were robbed by strangers. When the facts don’t add up, Lt. Joe Kenda and his team go on the hunt for a secret eyewitness they’ve heard could crack the case wide open.

programme.title: Homicide Hunter - My Second Case - E701
programme.desc: A woman’s mangled body is found beside a lonely stretch of highway. When the coroner suspects foul play, Kenda is called in to solve the second homicide case of his career. But along the way, the rookie detective will learn a painful lesson.

programme.desc: Jaime deals blackjack aboard a floating casino carrying unstable, explosive energy-cell prototypes.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime competes as a professional lady wrestler while searching for a missing OSI agent.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime poses as a singer to find out what happened to a missing OSI agent.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime combats robot replicas of OSI secretaries who are plotting to kidnap Oscar Goldman.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime and Steve become Oscar's only hope of survival as Dr. Franklin repels a military strike force with a weather machine.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: On a refueling stop at a remote island, Jaime and a scientist (Rick Lenz) connect mysterious disappearances to a meteorite.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime dons a nun's habit to break a diamond-smuggling ring using a convent winery as a drop-off point.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime is unaware that the foreign agent she is seeking has spotted her first, and ordered her execution.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime enrolls as a police academy cadet to locate a foreign agent known to be a member of the class.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: An OSI cryptographer (Peter Haskell), angry about funding cuts, flees with the coding analyzer he invented.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Part 1 of 2. Jaime is pitted against a computer devised by a scientist to blackmail the world into lasting peace.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: The supercomputer controlling the doomsday device begins to appreciate wounded Jaime's skill and courage.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime regains consciousness in a prison cell after having been switched with her surgically created look-alike.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime is unable to convince anyone of her identity after her escape from jail.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime works as tutor to a difficult prince (Lance Kerwin) to protect his father, a Middle East oil magnate, from assassins.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime seeks to befriend the withdrawn daughter of a Vietnam war veteran who hasn't spoken since her mother's death.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime travels to Paris with an art forger to trap a master criminal .

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime is frightened by an Indian burial demon that confronts her while she's visiting an Indian lore expert.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: This series is based on the adventures of Jamie Sommers, who almost dies while sky diving. She is rebuilt bionically, just like her former fiance, Steve Austin (the six million dollar man himself). Grateful for being saved, Jamie agrees to work for the government and puts her bionic skills to work on dangerous missions.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime masquerades as a bank robber to capture the leaders of a big-time theft racket.

programme.title: The Bionic Woman
programme.desc: Jaime discovers the existence of the world's first bionic dog and has just five days to save it from destruction.

programme.title: The Rapid City Rapist
programme.desc: In South Dakota, 60-year-old Gwen Miller, a pharmacist, fails to show up for work. Co-workers find she has been strangled and raped.

programme.title: A Family Torn Apart
programme.desc: Megan and Sherri Scherer are found dead in their home, Megan had also been raped. Later that evening another woman is shot and wounded at her home.

programme.title: Justice for Leslie
programme.desc: Leslie Penrod Harris leaves a restaurant after arguing with her husband. Hours later her naked body is found near El Toro Air Base 20 miles away.

programme.title: Cuyahoga Falls Mystery
programme.desc: The nude body of 17 year old Barbara Blatnik is found face down on a rural road. She had been violently raped and strangled.

programme.title: Chilling Notes From a Killer
programme.desc: Janet Tinsley reports her 8-year-old daughter April missing after she fails to return home. Three days later a man out jogging discovers April's body.

programme.title: Remembering Stevie
programme.desc: In 1963, a man fishing reels in the body of a toddler. It isn't for 57 years after the discovery in 2020 that the identity is revealed.

programme.title: Date Night Murder in Michigan
programme.desc: Terry Wood comes home to find his wife Roxanne, lying dead in a pool of blood. She has two deep cuts carved into her neck and has suffered blunt force trauma.

programme.title: Carla's Last Valentines
programme.desc: 17-year old Carla Walker is with her boyfriend Rodney in his car when suddenly the door is ripped open by an unknown assailant.

programme.title: Last Seen at Dairy Queen
programme.desc: 16-year-old high school student Kim Bryant is last seen outside a Dairy Queen restaurant. Three weeks later, her body is discovered by three teenage boys.

programme.title: The Coat Hanger Killer
programme.desc: Mum of two Linda Slaten is found murdered in her bedroom in her Lakeland, Florida apartment. She'd been sexually assaulted while her children slept.

programme.title: The Mystery of the Headphones
programme.desc: 22-year-old Diana Hanson fails to return home from jogging in Las Vegas. Her worried parents call police.

programme.title: Little Miss Nobody
programme.desc: The decomposing body of a little girl is found in the Arizona desert. Detectives are unable to identify her, so the local community lays her to rest.

programme.title: The Slaying of Sylvia Quayle
programme.desc: The body of Sylvia Quayle is discovered by her distraught father in her Cherry Hills home. She's been shot, stabbed and sexually assaulted.

programme.title: Valentine's Day Murder
programme.desc: A young woman is last seen alive hitchhiking on Valentines Day. The next day her body is discovered along a deserted road; she's been strangled to death.

programme.title: The Mystery of the Parks
programme.desc: 12-year-old Michella Welch goes missing in Puget Park. That night, police locate her badly bludgeoned body. There is evidence of sexual assault.

programme.title: Murder by the Base
programme.desc: The bruised and bloodied body of 25-year-old Naval recruit Pamela Cahanes is found in an abandoned lot near the Naval Training Centre.

programme.title: The Schoolbag in the Road
programme.desc: Stephanie Isaacson sets off on her walk to school; she never makes it. That evening her family's fears are confirmed, the 14-year-old girl's body is discovered.

programme.title: Her Last New Years Eve
programme.desc: The body of Tonya McKinley is lying on the side of a city street. She has been sexually assaulted, and it's clear the young mother had fought for her life.

programme.title: Dancing with Death
programme.desc: The naked body of Darlene Krashoc is discovered by two patrol officers behind a restaurant. Hardened investigators are shocked at the brutality of this murder.

programme.title: The Mint Box Murder
programme.desc: Nine-year-old Candy Rogers leaves home to sell scout mints in Spokane Washington. Two weeks later her body is discovered - she has been strangled.

programme.title: Delta Dawn Doe
programme.desc: Deputies from Jackson County Sheriff's Department discover the body of a drowned female toddler along the Escatawpa River in Mississippi.

programme.title: The Telephone Cord Killer
programme.desc: Michelle Wyatt's neighbours hear screams from her condo but don't investigate. The next day, her roommate finds Michelle's body just beyond the front door.

programme.title: Horror by the Roadside
programme.desc: A man discovers the body of a young woman in a roadside ditch in Kentucky. The girl is identified as 16-year-old Carol Sue Klaber, last seen riding her bike.

programme.title: The Court Reporter Murder
programme.desc: October 1970, Sacramento, California. 28-year-old court reporter Nancy Bennallack fails to show up for work, and her colleagues become worried.

programme.title: Stabbing in Sacramento
programme.desc: April, 1980. When Robin Brooks fails to show up for work, they go to her Sacramento apartment to check on her and are horrified to find her laying dead.

programme.title: Murder on Elm Street
programme.desc: July 1987, Carlsbad, New Mexico, Donna Hyatt's daughter returns home to find her mother murdered. She had been beaten, sexually assaulted and strangled.

programme.title: The Mammoth Lakes Murder
programme.desc: A man walking his dog California's Sierra Nevada mountains finds a human skull. Despite law enforcement's best efforts, they can't identify the woman's remains.

programme.title: Murder by I-59
programme.desc: In December, 1988, the tranquillity of smalltown life is shattered forever when the body of a woman is found by a group of road workers on the interstate.

programme.title: The South Lake Tahoe Strangler
programme.desc: In Sierra Nevada, 1977, a horseback ride turns into a nightmare when a group of riders discover a woman's dead body, discarded amongst the scenery.

programme.title: The Murder of Little Marise
programme.desc: In 1964, nine-year-old Marise Chiverella leaves for school. Her family say goodbye to her, not knowing that they will never see her again.

programme.title: The Huntington Beach Body
programme.desc: In California, a group of schoolboys find what they think is a scarecrow, but the reality is much worse - it is the body of a woman who has been murdered.

programme.title: Mommy Has Been Murdered
programme.desc: Compelling crime series. Investigative genetic genealogy is used to resolve the 1988 murder of a mother killed in front of her toddler.

programme.title: The Phoenix Canal Killer
programme.desc: Compelling crime series. Cutting-edge DNA science finally names the Phoenix Canal Killer who terrorised the city in the early 90s.

programme.title: Double Homicide in the OC
programme.desc: Compelling crime series. Forensic science reveals the name of a serial killer who murdered two women in the late 80s, 30 years later.

programme.title: Mississippi Rapist
programme.desc: In Rankin County, Mississippi in 1990, a woman is kidnapped and raped at knifepoint. Police are unable to identify the perpetrator.

programme.title: Justice Delayed
programme.desc: In Snohomish County in 1972, a young woman is discovered covered in blood by the road. She is taken to hospital where she passes away a short time later.

programme.title: Murder in Apartment 101
programme.desc: In Willoughby, Ohio in 1980, Mark Madger comes home to find his wife Nadine lying in a pool of her own blood with a kitchen knife embedded in her chest.

programme.title: Carrie's Courage
programme.desc: In 1985, a young woman is awoken by an intruder in her apartment, who steals her valuables and sexually assaults her at gunpoint.

programme.title: A Sadistic Killer
programme.desc: Compelling crime series. Investigative genetic genealogy unmasks the sexual deviant who raped and killed Christina Castiglione in 1982.

programme.title: Murder in Marietta
programme.desc: Compelling crime series. The 1972 rape and murder of nine-year-old Debbie Lynn Randall is solved thanks to science 50 years later.

programme.title: The Body in the Blanket
programme.desc: Compelling crime series using witness testimony and new interviews. Detectives take on the unsolved murder of Sharon Hammack.

programme.title: Evil Angel
programme.desc: Compelling crime series using witness testimony and new interviews. Police use new technology to find a perp of a brutal rape.

programme.title: The Book Store Murder
programme.desc: Compelling crime series using witness testimony and new interviews. DNA Detectives solve a murder of a great-grandma in Utah.

programme.title: The McClintock Park Murders
programme.desc: Compelling crime series. Forensic investigative genetic genealogy solves the 1987 double murder of a young couple in Wisconsin.

programme.title: Strangled in the Sand
programme.desc: Police solve the decades-old cold case of Clare Holman through new advancements in DNA technology.

programme.title: Terror in Garden Grove
programme.desc: In 1976, 19-year-old Janet Stallcup goes missing while on her way to a party. Eight days later, her body is found in her car.

programme.title: The Runaway Murder
programme.desc: In 1978, the body of 16-year-old Krisann Baxter is found in Washington. Investigators try to find Krisann's killer, but don't find any answers.

programme.title: Justice for Krista
programme.desc: Krista Martin's life is tragically cut short because of an intruder. A friend finds her and calls 911, starting an investigation that spans four decades.

programme.title: The Imposter Rapist
programme.desc: In Chandler, Arizona in 1991, an intruder viciously sexually assaults a woman in her own home. The case goes unsolved for decades.

programme.title: The Schoolteacher Murder
programme.desc: The parents of Catherine Edwards find her body in her bathroom. The killer evades justice, that is, until forensic science catches up with him.

programme.title: The Murder on Thumb Butte
programme.desc: Will a new forensic science tool find the killer of Cathy Sposito, murdered on an Arizona hiking trail in 1987?

programme.title: Terror in Texas
programme.desc: Susan Eads is found murdered in Texas in 1983. Decades later, can modern forensics finally find the perpetrator?

programme.title: Home Invasion Homicide
programme.desc: In 1986, Barbara Carr was killed in a home invasion, while her husband escaped. Will new science finally unearth a suspect?

programme.title: Downtown After Dark
programme.desc: Years after a murder in 1991, will determination and new forensic tools finally find Danielle Clause's killer?

programme.title: Finding Suzanne
programme.desc: Human remains found in 1994 start a long search to identify Suzanne Kjellenberg and a killer. New forensics may give answers.

programme.title: Murder in Green Bay
programme.desc: In 1986, police struggle to find a young mother's killer. Will new forensic investigative tools hold the answer?

programme.title: A Murder In Lexington
programme.desc: When mother Mary Davis is found murdered, the case spans decades. Bleeding edge forensics could hold the answers.

programme.title: The Ramsey Street Rapist
programme.desc: Serial rapes spur fear in a city in North Carolina. Years later new forensic science finds the perpetrator.

programme.title: Murder on Edgewater Creek Bridge
programme.desc: Can forensic science solve the murder of Melissa Lee, which baffled Washington detectives in 1993?

programme.title: Brutality in Brownwood
programme.desc: A woman in Texas is killed and left in an old cellar. Can new forensic science tools find the murderer?

programme.title: Murder in the Median
programme.desc: In 2024, Pamela Wittman, a 25-year-old from Indiana, was identified, solving the 1980 Daytona Beach cold case linked to a serial killer.

programme.title: Jane Doe by the Road
programme.desc: Found shot in 1986, Maria Pilar Del Gadillo Carrillo remained unidentified until 2024, when authorities used genetic genealogy and reopened her case.

programme.title: Murder on Highway 243
programme.desc: Esther Gonzalez was killed in 1979 while walking in Riverside. Randy Williamson lived freely until 2014. In 2023, forensic genealogy closed the cold case.

programme.title: A Forensic Gamechanger
programme.desc: In 1991, 16-year-old Sarah Yarborough was murdered outside her school. Eyewitnesses saw a man - but it took nearly 30 years and forensic genealogy to find him.

programme.title: The Suspect List
programme.desc: Compelling crime series. DNA and genealogy reveal serial killer Jerry McFadden murdered Anna Hlavka in 1979 Portland case.

programme.title: Murder Between Floors
programme.desc: Found murdered in a Seattle garage in July 1967, Susan Galvin remained without justice until 2018, when DNA and genetic genealogy identified her killer.

programme.title: Uncovered Truths
programme.desc: In October 2003, the San Diego County community was shaken by a tragic discovery: the dismembered legs of a woman were found in a dumpster.

programme.title: Celebrating the Corban Festival
programme.desc: Kashgar, situated in the southwest of Xinjiang, was a key stop on the ancient Silk Road. The Corban Festival began here with the arrival of Islam in the 7th century AD, and has developed into a traditional holiday celebrated by everyone in Kashgar, just as important as Spring Festival. Locals load their tables with food to reward themselves for a year of hard work, and celebrate a tradition of sharing and generosity.

programme.title: PODCAST: When influencer culture meets ancient lakeside town - the changing face of Dali
programme.desc: Filming at a lakeside village in China's picturesque Dali prefecture, Travelogue hosts Tianran He, Jack Klumpp and Alex McCutcheon find themselves at an establishment that is two parts coffee house, eight parts photography studio, swarming with professional photographers and dedicated influencers all striving for that perfect cover photo against the shimmering Erhai Lake. They reflect on the almost mystical allure that has led travelers, past and present, to fall in love with Dali and never want to leave. Over an elegantly served Americano, they discuss how coffee production, redevelopment, and modern tourism trends are reshaping this idyllic corner of the world.

programme.title: Aerial China IV: Henan
programme.desc: Perhaps there’s no place that epitomises the cultural grandeur of China’s central plains than Henan. A cradle of Chinese civilization, abounding with resources and talented people, this is a place that has thousands of years of history in every corner. programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people's southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media - Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Brian Linden: Take me home, country roads
programme.desc: Since first arriving in China in 1984, Brian Linden has built a bond with the country that now spans more than four decades. For over 20 years, he has been rooted in Xizhou, a historic town in Yunnan. Drawn by Eastern culture, he arrived as an outsider but gradually became a dedicated rural builder. Though he has traveled to more than 120 countries, Linden ultimately chose to settle in rural southwest China. What inspired him to stay, and what China story does he hope to share with the world? Follow Linden's journey as we explore his life in rural China.

programme.title: Wudang Martial Arts & Taichi
programme.desc: Join host Yegor on a journey into the heart of China's Wudang Mountains, the spiritual cradle of Taoism, to explore the philosophy, techniques, and living spirit of Wudang Quan and Tai chi. From the internal cultivation of qi to the harmony between body and mind, Wudang martial arts are more than just physical training - they are a way of life rooted in the Tao.

programme.title: Four Faces of Muqam
programme.desc: Muqam is a performing art with its roots in the folklore of Xinjiang. Rather like an encyclopedia, Muqam is a record of the history and lifestyle of the local Uygur people. It originated in folk culture, with lyrics that covered everything from philosophical aphorisms to folk tales. Muqam is an integral part of Xinjiang culture, a vehicle for Uygur people to express their feelings and ideas.

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China.In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui...

programme.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named "Duck Poo Fragrance" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional "yum cha" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling "kueh" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Wujiang: The Land of Silk
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Wujiang District of Suzhou City on China's east coast to explore the birthplace of silk. There we discover that silk is not merely a precious fabric but also a way of life. For centuries, Wujiang District has been one of China's largest‑scale silk‑producing regions, which has turned it into a major commercial hub. Local residents worship a distinctive deity‑the Silkworm Goddess. Per the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, the Lesser Fullness of Grain (Xiaoman) solar term coincides with the goddess's birthday. Local folk opera troupes take turns staging performances on the stage by the main temple hall over several days to mark the occasion and pray for good...
